title: CLO 2025.0 - Virtual Model IK Joint Mapping
description: In version 2025.0, with the IK joint mapping feature for virtual models, you can more easily realize your designs using various virtual models in CLO.
transcript:
This video introduces the virtual model IK joint printing function for you.  
In this version, we have introduced the virtual model IK joint printing function.  
This function allows virtual models imported from outside to use the actions and postures provided by Clo.  
So let's take a look at the IK joint printing function together.  

IK joint printing is currently only supported for FBX files with Google information.  
First, we need to import an FBX file to print the IK joint.  
Before importing, we need to explain some important points to note before printing IK.  
FBX files should not have repeated joint names.  
In addition, virtual models must include joints such as shoulders, elbows, wrists, pelvis, knees, and ankles.  
T-position is the standard reference position for IK printing.  
IK printing with incorrect positioning may lead to errors.  
Therefore,  
it is necessary to correctly set the virtual model to T-position.  
If the virtual model is not in T-position,  
it is necessary to manually adjust the joint points of the virtual model in the 3D window to T-position.  
In the virtual model information display in the 3D vertical menu bar,  
open the virtual model joint points,  
then select the joint points of the virtual model,  
and adjust the virtual model to T-position.  
It is necessary to note that  
for non-humanoid images or quadruped virtual models,  
IK printing may not be correctly applied.  

Now,  
let us print the IK joints on the virtual model.  
In the main menu bar,  
find the virtual model editor under the virtual model section,  
then select the IK joint option tab.  
Now our virtual model is already in T-position.  
Next,  
press the "Set T-position" button in the upper right corner  
to confirm the adjusted T-position.  
If the setting is completed according to the above steps,  
the "Reset Position" button on the right will be activated.  
After adjusting the position during the IK printing process,  
the "Reset Position" button can help you restore the original position.  

Next,  
let's print the joints.  
There are two main ways to print the joints.  
You can manually print each joint,  
or you can automatically print the joints by identifying the joint names.  
First,  
let's see how to manually print joints according to the joint list.  
Let's look at the joint list first.  
The joint printing is divided into the "Required" and "Selected" categories.  
The corresponding joint names are listed under each category.  
To ensure that IK joint printing is accurate,  
you must print all the joints in the required category.  
For the selected category,  
although it is not mandatory,  
if the virtual model has these joints,  
you can print them to present more accurate movements and positions.  

Now,  
let's carefully print the joints of the required category.  
First,  
when you click on the name of a joint,  
you can check the preview at the top  
to see the location of the selected joint on the virtual model.  
You can also directly click on the joint in the preview  
to find the corresponding position.  
Next,  
select the corresponding joint in the 3D window,  
or you can first click on the joint in the virtual model,  
then click on the project in the option tab to print it.  
I will print it from the top.  
If multiple joints overlap,  
you can choose which joint to print.  
After printing,  
the printed area will be displayed in the preview of the 3D window  
and the virtual model editor in green.  
In the joint list,  
there will be a white highlight on the left side of the joint,  
indicating that the joint printing is complete.  
In addition,  
the name of the joint saved for the virtual model  
will be displayed next to the printing box on the right.  
If you misprinted the joint  
and want to re-select the joint to be printed,  
you can select the joint in the joint list,  
or the joint in the preview,  
then click on another joint to re-print it.  
Or you can also select the joint in the joint list,  
or the joint in the preview,  
then press the Delete key on the keyboard to delete it,  
and then re-select the correct joint point.  

Now,  
let's pay attention to the remaining joints.  
You can see that when printing the left joint,  
the right one is also printed.  
This is because symmetrical printing  
is not activated in the upper right corner of the virtual model editor.  
Therefore,  
even if you print one side of the joint,  
it will automatically identify and print the corresponding joint on the other side.  
Please note that  
if you want to automatically use symmetrical printing,  
the joint names must indicate left and right,  
or use the letters L and R (uppercase or lowercase),  
with an underscore dividing left and right.  
You can select the joint point,  
and then modify the name in the virtual editor.  
If you do not enable symmetrical printing,  
you need to manually print the left and right joints separately.  

Now let's continue to print all the remaining joints below.  
Once all the joints in the required category are printed,  
the status on the right side of the project will show as complete,  
indicating that IK printing is finished.  

Next, let's see how to automatically print the joints.  
Before automatically printing the joints,  
press the reset button at the top  
to reset all the joints printed so far.  
When you press the "Auto-print" button at the bottom,  
all the required joints under the required category will be automatically printed.  
You can see that the status is also displayed as complete.  
But what you need to pay attention to is that  
only when the joint names of the virtual model  
match the joint names in the virtual model list,  
or the virtual model file is from  
DeathMiximoCharacterCreator or MetaHuman,  
will the auto-printing function work normally.  

Next, let's take a look at  
how to save the information of the IK joint printing.  
The IK joint printing information of the virtual model  
can be saved as an IKS file.  
You can click on "Save and Open" in the upper right corner,  
and save the IK data as an IKS file,  
or open a previously saved IKS file.  
After completing all the joint printing,  
you can directly apply the available postures.  
What needs to be explained is that  
IKS files only work for virtual models with the same structure,  
and are compatible between virtual models using the same printing method.  
You can see that the posture has been correctly applied.  
The virtual model file with IK joint printing can be saved in a virtual model format for later use.  
Next time you can use it directly.  

By using the new IK joint printing function in the virtual model editor,  
you can more easily use various virtual models in Clo to realize your designs.

chunks.content: # CLO 2025.0 - Virtual Model IK Joint Mapping This document explains the virtual model IK (Inverse Kinematics) joint printing function introduced in CLO 2025.0. It covers supported file formats, prerequisites for virtual models, detailed procedures for manual and automatic IK joint printing, symmetrical printing considerations, and saving IK joint data for reuse. --- ## Overview of Virtual Model IK Joint Printing This section introduces the virtual model IK joint printing feature, which enables imported virtual models to use CLO's action and posture systems via IK joint mapping. The function currently supports FBX files containing Google information and requires proper preparation of the virtual model. --- ## Requirements and Preparations for IK Joint Printing This section details the necessary conditions for successfully printing IK joints on virtual models, including file format constraints, joint naming rules, and model positioning prerequisites. - **Supported File Format:** - Only FBX files with Google information are supported for IK joint printing. - **Joint Naming and Presence:** - FBX files must not have repeated joint names. - Virtual models must include essential joints: shoulders, elbows, wrists, pelvis, knees, and ankles. - **Reference Pose (T-Position):** - The T-position is the standard reference pose for IK joint printing. - Incorrectly positioned models will cause errors during IK printing. - Virtual models must be adjusted to T-position before printing. This can be done manually by selecting and adjusting joint points in the 3D window. - **Limitations:** - IK joint printing may not function correctly for non-humanoid or quadruped virtual models. --- ## Using the Virtual Model Editor for IK Joint Printing This section explains how to access the IK joint printing tools and prepare the model within CLO. 1. Navigate to the **Virtual Model Editor** via the main menu under the virtual model section. 2. Select the **IK Joint** tab. 3. Confirm the virtual model is in T-position. If adjustments are needed: - Use the **Set T-position** button to lock the pose. - The **Reset Position** button becomes active after setting T-position, allowing restoration to the original pose during the printing process. --- ## Manual IK Joint Printing Procedure This section provides step-by-step instructions for manually assigning joints for IK mapping. - **Joint Categories:** - **Required Joints:** Must be printed for accurate IK functionality. - **Selected Joints:** Optional joints that improve movement accuracy if present. - **Printing Steps:** 1. Review the joint list divided into Required and Selected categories. 2. Click a joint name to see its location preview on the virtual model. You can also select the joint directly in the preview or 3D window. 3. Select the corresponding joint on the model in the 3D window or virtual model editor, then click "Print" in the option tab. 4. If multiple joints overlap, choose the correct one to print. 5. Printed joints appear highlighted in green in the 3D window and editor preview. 6. The joint list shows a white highlight indicating printing completion, and the virtual model's saved joint name appears next to the print box. 7.

chunks.content: You can also select the joint directly in the preview or 3D window. 3. Select the corresponding joint on the model in the 3D window or virtual model editor, then click "Print" in the option tab. 4. If multiple joints overlap, choose the correct one to print. 5. Printed joints appear highlighted in green in the 3D window and editor preview. 6. The joint list shows a white highlight indicating printing completion, and the virtual model's saved joint name appears next to the print box. 7. To correct a misprint, select the joint in the list or preview, then either print a different joint or press Delete to remove and reprint the joint. --- ## Symmetrical Joint Printing This section explains how symmetrical printing works and how to configure joint names to enable it. - Symmetrical printing automatically prints the corresponding joint on the opposite side when one side is printed. - It is **disabled by default**; when off, left and right joints must be printed manually. - To enable symmetrical printing, activate the option in the upper right corner of the virtual model editor. - Joint names must clearly indicate left and right sides, typically using "L" and "R" (case-insensitive) or spelled-out terms, separated by an underscore (e.g., "arm_L", "arm_R"). - Joint names can be edited in the virtual model editor to comply with this naming convention. --- ## Automatic IK Joint Printing This section describes the automatic joint printing feature and important conditions for its use. - Before auto-printing, press the **Reset Position** button to clear any previously printed joints. - Press the **Auto-print** button to automatically assign all required joints. - Auto-printing works only if: - Joint names in the virtual model exactly match those in the virtual model joint list, **or** - The virtual model originates from **DeathMiximoCharacterCreator** or **MetaHuman**. - Upon completion, the status displays as complete. --- ## Saving and Applying IK Joint Data This section outlines how to save IK joint printing data and reuse it on compatible models. - IK joint printing information can be saved as an **IKS file**. - Use the **Save and Open** button in the upper right corner to save the current IK data or load a previously saved IKS file. - IKS files only work with virtual models of the same structure and compatible printing methods. - After loading IK data, you can directly apply postures to the virtual model, confirming correct mapping. - The virtual model file, along with IK joint printing data, can be saved in CLO’s native virtual model format for future use. --- ## Benefits of the IK Joint Printing Function This final section emphasizes the advantages of the new IK joint printing feature. - Enables easier integration of diverse virtual models into CLO’s design environment. - Facilitates the use of CLO’s built-in actions and postures on imported models. - Improves accuracy and flexibility in virtual model animation and posture application.
